sn12.37:1.2: “Bhikkhus, this body is not yours, nor does it belong to others.
sn12.37:1.3: It is old kamma, to be seen as generated and fashioned by volition, as something to be felt.
sn12.37:2.1: Therein, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple attends carefully and closely to dependent origination itself thus:
sn12.37:2.2: ‘When this exists, that comes to be; with the arising of this, that arises.
sn12.37:2.3: When this does not exist, that does not come to be; with the cessation of this, that ceases. That is,
sn12.37:2.4: with ignorance as condition, volitional formations come to be;
sn12.37:2.5: with volitional formations as condition, consciousness….
sn12.37:2.6: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.37:2.7: But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance comes cessation of volitional formations; with the cessation of volitional formations,
sn12.37:2.9: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
